speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I understand you are experiencing progressive difficulty with walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To help me narrow down the cause, can you describe exactly when these symptoms started and whether they have been worsening gradually or in steps?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. I would like to check for any accompanying cognitive changes, such as memory loss or personality changes, and also ask if you have noticed any tremors or muscle stiffness in your limbs.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You have mentioned rigidity, a mild tremor, and orthostatic hypotension alongside your walking and urinary issues. Do you experience any visual hallucinations or sudden episodes of falling backward?
